description: The LLD concept graph. Every rubric criterion and every drill maps to one or more of these. Mastery is tracked per concept, not per problem. Prerequisite edges gate the next-best-action recommender.

tiers.foundation: Ideas everything else is built on. No prerequisites.
tiers.behaviour: How objects change and interact over time.

concepts.name: Encapsulation
concepts.plain: A class hides its internal state and exposes behaviour instead of data.
concepts.tell: Getters and setters on every field; callers mutating internals directly.

concepts.name: Abstraction
concepts.plain: Model only what matters for the problem; leave the rest out.
concepts.tell: Classes carrying fields nothing in the design ever reads.

concepts.name: Cohesion
concepts.plain: Everything inside a class belongs to the same job.
concepts.tell: A responsibility sentence that needs the word 'and' more than once.

concepts.name: Coupling
concepts.plain: How much one class must know about another to work.
concepts.tell: Long reach-through chains like a.getB().getC().doThing().

concepts.name: Association Modelling
concepts.plain: Choosing correctly between owns-a, has-a, uses-a and is-a.
concepts.tell: Everything drawn as has-a because the distinction was never considered.

concepts.name: Domain Modelling
concepts.plain: Naming classes after real things in the problem, and telling entities from values.
concepts.tell: Class names like DataManager or InfoHandler that name no real concept.

concepts.name: Single Responsibility
concepts.plain: A class should have one reason to change.
concepts.tell: A god class named *Manager or *Service that touches everything.

concepts.name: Interface Design
concepts.plain: A contract that says what, never how, and is hard to misuse.
concepts.tell: Interfaces that leak their implementation in method names or return types.

concepts.name: Polymorphism
concepts.plain: Different types answering the same message in their own way.
concepts.tell: switch or if-else chains on a type field.

concepts.name: Open/Closed
concepts.plain: Add behaviour by adding code, not by editing working code.
concepts.tell: Every new feature means another branch inside an existing method.

concepts.name: Liskov Substitution
concepts.plain: A subtype must work anywhere its parent does, without surprises.
concepts.tell: An override that throws UnsupportedOperation, or tightens what the parent accepted.

concepts.name: Interface Segregation
concepts.plain: Small focused contracts beat one fat one.
concepts.tell: Implementers stubbing out methods they do not need.

concepts.name: Dependency Inversion
concepts.plain: Depend on abstractions; let the concrete thing be handed in.
concepts.tell: new ConcreteThing() inside a constructor of a high-level class.

concepts.name: Composition over Inheritance
concepts.plain: Prefer assembling behaviour from parts over inheriting it.
concepts.tell: Deep hierarchies, or subclasses created just to vary one value.

concepts.name: State Modelling
concepts.plain: Making the legal lifecycle explicit instead of implied by flags.
concepts.tell: Several booleans that must agree, like isPaid plus isShipped plus isCancelled.

concepts.name: Immutability & Value Objects
concepts.plain: Values that never change are safe to share and easy to reason about.
concepts.tell: Money or Date passed around as a mutable object with setters.

concepts.name: Error Modelling
concepts.plain: Treat failure as part of the domain, not an afterthought.
concepts.tell: Returning null or false to mean five different problems.

concepts.name: Testability
concepts.plain: A design you can test without standing up the world.
concepts.tell: Business logic that cannot run without a clock, a network or a database.

concepts.name: Extensibility
concepts.plain: Putting the seam where the requirement will actually change.
concepts.tell: Abstractions everywhere except the one place the spec said varies.

concepts.name: Concurrency Safety
concepts.plain: Shared state stays correct when two things happen at once.
concepts.tell: check-then-act on shared state with no guard around it.
